digest.component_or_area: bridge interface layer: CLI, MCP, and Python library
propositions: New noun-based bridge operations (preview, sync, status, pause, resume, check_access) must be exposed through the public library and registered as MCP tools with explicit typed inputs and output schemas.
Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck must remain callable with unchanged signatures, defaults, return types, exceptions, and mutation boundaries as compatibility entrypoints.
Typed library and MCP operations must reuse the canonical run_pass() / _Disposition classification seam rather than duplicating reconciler logic or invoking the CLI subprocess.
Every mutating bridge operation (sync, pause, resume, and legacy reconcile mutating modes) must be gated by mcp.allow_jira_sync; read-only operations must not be gated beyond existing authorization.
Compatibility adapters must preserve published defaults (reconcile defaults to dry-run), accepted mode values, and mutation boundaries—preview must never silently become sync.
New MCP tools must publish output schemas, update model/type registries, and pass schema parity checks; existing compatibility tool schemas must remain valid.
